newsitem.title: MEXICO: CAMBIOR, LUISMIN POSTPONE MINE DECISION TIL SEPT.
newsitem.headline: CAMBIOR, LUISMIN POSTPONE MINE DECISION TIL SEPT.

text.p: Canada-based miner Cambior Inc and Mexican partner Industrias Luismin postponed to September a decision on the construction of a pilot gold mine in Mexico's Durango state.

"It (the decision) was not taken in July, but there is going to be a meeting in three weeks between Cambior and Luismin to define (when construction will start)," a Luismin director told Reuters Tuesday.

Luismin, a unit of Sanluis Corporacion announced in June the decision on the companies' Metates project would be made in July. Metates is classified as a world-class gold mine. The joint venture is 50-50.

The director said the delay did not amount to a cancelation of the project. "No way, everything continues as normal," he said, adding gold and zinc content results were still being taken and studied from Metates.

Cambior and Luismin will meet in the United States next month to thrash out an accord on investment participation in the pilot project, he added. "Whoever foots the money, the (initial pilot project investment) is around $12 million," he said.
Plans are to work a pilot project at Metates for at least 18 months and over two rainy seasons to justify a full-scale mining operation.
